styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: Pebble beaches, sea swims and sunset walks along the Promenade.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Socca, market stalls and seafront dinners in the Old Town.

styles.label: Old Town
styles.blurb: Narrow lanes, baroque churches and the Cours Saleya market.

stays.why: Walk to the Old Town lanes, Cours Saleya market and the seafront; best for food lovers, but streets are narrow and lively at night.
Sea views and the beach are right outside; a short walk to the Old Town and tram line 2 at the airport route.
Quiet shopping streets between the station and the sea; good value and an easy tram ride to the airport.
Leafy hill district with the Matisse and Chagall museums; calmer nights but a steeper walk or a bus or taxi to the sea.

food: Try socca, a thin chickpea flour pancake, at a counter in the Old Town. Eat it hot and sold by the slice.
Visit the Cours Saleya market in the morning for fruit, cheese and olives. Check the day, as the market hours change in winter.
Order pissaladière (onion tart) and pan bagnat (tuna roll) for a cheap lunch. Expect about €6-12 at a simple bakery.
Book seafront or Old Town dinners ahead in summer. Prices vary a lot, so check the menu before you sit down.
Stay away from restaurants with staff outside calling you in. Walk a few streets off the main square for better food.
more_time: Take a bus trip to Monaco or Eze for a half day. Lignes d'Azur buses cost €1.70 a ride, so validate each trip.
Spend a day in Cannes or Antibes. Check bus or train times on the day, as schedules change.
Go to Corsica for a longer break. Ferries run from Nice port, so check local schedules before you go.

recommend.why: Two nights give you time for the Old Town, one beach day and a museum visit without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: Cool, about 5-13°C, with around 6 rain days. Good for museums and quiet city walks.
Feb: Still cool, about 6-13°C, with around 7 rain days. Pack a warm layer for evenings.
Mar: Mild, about 7-15°C, with around 7 rain days. Spring starts; sights are quieter.
Apr: Pleasant, about 10-18°C, with around 8 rain days. Good for walking and first sea views.
May: Warm, about 14-21°C, with around 9 rain days. A strong time for the Old Town and fewer crowds.
Jun: Warm, about 18-25°C, with around 7 rain days. Beach season begins; book stays early.
Jul: Hot, about 21-28°C, with around 3 rain days. Busy and sunny; swim early or late.
Aug: Hottest, about 21-29°C, with around 4 rain days. Peak crowds and prices; plan shade breaks.
Sep: Warm, about 18-25°C, with around 6 rain days. Sea is still warm and crowds ease.
Oct: Mild, about 14-21°C, with around 9 rain days. Good for food and culture; pack a light rain jacket.
Nov: Cool, about 9-16°C, with around 9 rain days. Quieter streets and fewer beach days.
Dec: Cool, about 6-14°C, with around 6 rain days. Quiet city; check opening hours before you go.

climate_guide.summary: Mild Mediterranean climate: warm, sunny summers and mild winters, with rain spread across the year.

items.title: Best time: May to June and September
items.text: Highs of about 21-25°C and fewer rain days than autumn. Good for walking and the beach.

items.title: Hot summers (July and August)
items.text: Highs of 28-29°C and the fewest rain days, around 3-4. Go to the beach early and rest in the afternoon.

items.title: Wettest in May and October
items.text: About 9 rain days a month. Keep a compact umbrella and plan museum visits for showery days.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: Lows of about 5-7°C from December to February. Bring a warm jacket for evenings by the sea.

items.title: Shoulder seasons
items.text: April and October are mild, with highs of 18-21°C. Good for sightseeing with smaller crowds.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for changing temperatures, comfortable walking shoes for the hills, sun hat and sunscreen for summer, and a light rain jacket for autumn.

transit.best: Tram line 2 to the airport and centre, then walk the Old Town and seafront.

modes.text: No metro in Nice. Use tram line 2 and buses instead.
Lignes d'Azur buses charge €1.70 a ride, with a transfer allowed within 74 minutes. Buy a top-up card or pay with contactless. Always validate.
Taxis are pricey and some overcharge. Uber and Bolt both operate, with a ride-share pick-up zone at the airport.
Driving is hard in the centre: one-way streets and scarce metered parking. Use an underground car park, roughly €8-10 a day.
The centre is walkable. Old Town and the seafront are close to each other.
Tram line 2 links the airport with the centre (Jean Médecin). It runs about every 8 minutes on weekdays, roughly 04:30 to after midnight.
Ferries run from Nice port to Corsica. Check local schedules before you go.
Shared bikes and e-scooters are available in parts of the city.
